description: This topic explains multimedia and its elements, computer graphics, raster and vector images, common media file formats, multimedia hardware and software, image editing operations, and the advantages and challenges of using multimedia.

mcq.questionText: Which term best describes the combination of text, images, sound, video and animation in a single application?
mcq.explanation: Multimedia means the use of more than one type of media, such as text, graphics, audio, video and animation, together in one program.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is NOT an element of multimedia?
mcq.explanation: Text, audio, video, graphics and animation are multimedia elements. A printer is an output device, not a media element.

mcq.questionText: An image made up of tiny coloured dots arranged in a grid is called a:
mcq.explanation: A raster or bitmap image is made of pixels (tiny dots) arranged in a grid, where each pixel stores a colour value.

mcq.questionText: Which type of graphic uses mathematical lines, curves and shapes so it can be scaled without losing quality?
mcq.explanation: Vector graphics are defined by mathematical formulas for points, lines and curves, so they can be resized without becoming blurred or pixelated.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a common file format for still images?
mcq.explanation: JPEG is a widely used image format. MP3 and WAV are audio formats, while MP4 is a video format.

mcq.questionText: Which file format is used mainly for audio (sound)?
mcq.explanation: MP3 is a popular compressed audio format. PNG, GIF and BMP are all image formats.

mcq.questionText: Which image format supports a transparent background and is often used for web graphics and logos?
mcq.explanation: PNG supports transparency and lossless compression, making it suitable for logos and web images.

mcq.questionText: The smallest single point that makes up a digital raster image is called a:
mcq.explanation: A pixel (picture element) is the smallest point in a digital image; many pixels together form the whole picture.

mcq.questionText: What does the term 'resolution' of an image normally refer to?

options.text: The number of pixels in the image

mcq.explanation: Resolution describes how many pixels make up an image (for example 1920 x 1080); more pixels usually mean more detail.

mcq.questionText: Colour depth of an image refers to:

options.text: How deep the file is stored on disk
The number of bits used to represent the colour of each pixel

mcq.explanation: Colour depth is the number of bits used per pixel; more bits allow more colours to be displayed.

mcq.questionText: Which software would you most likely use to edit and enhance photographs?
mcq.explanation: An image (photo) editor is used to crop, resize, retouch and adjust the colours of pictures.

mcq.questionText: Which device is used to convert a printed photograph or document into a digital image?
mcq.explanation: A scanner captures a printed image and turns it into a digital file that can be stored and edited on a computer.

mcq.questionText: Removing the unwanted outer parts of an image to keep only a chosen area is called:
mcq.explanation: Cropping trims away the edges of an image so that only the desired part remains.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a major challenge of using multimedia files?
mcq.explanation: Multimedia files, especially video and audio, are large and need a lot of storage and powerful hardware to process.

mcq.questionText: The use of multimedia in schools to make lessons more interesting through videos and sound is an example of multimedia in:
mcq.explanation: Using multimedia for teaching and learning, such as educational videos and interactive lessons, is an application in education.

fib.questionText: The combination of text, graphics, sound, video and animation in one application is called _____.
fib.explanation: Multimedia uses several media types together in a single program or presentation.

fib.questionText: The smallest dot that makes up a digital raster image is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A pixel is a single picture element; many pixels together form a complete bitmap image.

fib.questionText: Images made from mathematical lines and curves that can be resized without losing quality are called _____ graphics.
fib.explanation: Vector graphics use mathematical formulas, so they scale up or down without becoming blurred.

fib.questionText: An image made of a grid of coloured pixels is known as a raster or _____ image.
fib.explanation: Raster images are also called bitmap images because they are stored as a map of pixels.

fib.questionText: The common compressed audio file format that ends with the extension .mp3 is called _____.
fib.explanation: MP3 is a widely used audio format that compresses sound to save storage space.

fib.questionText: A device used to turn a printed picture into a digital image is a _____.
fib.explanation: A scanner reads a physical document or photo and creates a digital copy on the computer.

fib.questionText: The number of pixels that make up an image is referred to as the image _____.
fib.explanation: Resolution describes the amount of detail in an image, expressed as the number of pixels (for example 1280 x 720).

fib.questionText: The image editing operation that trims away unwanted edges of a picture is called _____.
fib.explanation: Cropping keeps only the chosen part of an image and removes the rest.

fib.questionText: A series of still images shown quickly to create the illusion of movement is called _____.
fib.explanation: Animation displays many frames in quick succession so that objects appear to move.

fib.questionText: The number of bits used to store the colour of each pixel is known as the colour _____.
fib.explanation: Colour depth measures how many bits represent each pixel; higher depth means more possible colours.

tf.questionText: Multimedia uses only text and nothing else.
tf.explanation: Multimedia combines several media types, including text, graphics, audio, video and animation, not just text.

tf.questionText: Vector graphics can be enlarged without becoming blurred or pixelated.
tf.explanation: Because vector graphics are based on mathematical formulas, they keep their quality at any size.

tf.questionText: MP4 is a common file format for video.
tf.explanation: MP4 is one of the most widely used video file formats.

tf.questionText: A pixel is the largest part of a video file.
tf.explanation: A pixel is the smallest single point of a digital image, not the largest part of a video.

tf.questionText: Higher image resolution generally means more detail but a larger file size.
tf.explanation: More pixels give more detail, which usually increases the storage space needed.

tf.questionText: WAV is an example of a video file format.
tf.explanation: WAV is an audio (sound) file format, not a video format.

tf.questionText: A speaker is an output device used to play sound in a multimedia system.
tf.explanation: Speakers output audio so that users can hear sound from multimedia content.

tf.questionText: Raster (bitmap) images usually lose quality and look blocky when they are greatly enlarged.
tf.explanation: Because raster images have a fixed number of pixels, enlarging them too much makes the pixels visible and the image blurry.

tf.questionText: Multimedia is used in advertising to make products more attractive to customers.
tf.explanation: Advertising uses images, video and sound to attract attention and promote products and services.

tf.questionText: One advantage of multimedia files is that they always use very little storage space.
tf.explanation: Multimedia files, especially audio and video, tend to be large and require a lot of storage space; this is a challenge, not an advantage.

summary.correctAnswer: Multimedia is the combination of two or more media types such as text, graphics, audio, video and animation in a single application.
summary.explanation: The key idea is the integration of several media types together rather than using only one.

summary.questionText: List the five main elements of multimedia.
summary.correctAnswer: Text, graphics (images), audio (sound), video, and animation.
summary.explanation: These are the standard building blocks of multimedia content.

summary.questionText: State three areas where multimedia is commonly applied.
summary.correctAnswer: Education, entertainment, and advertising (also business and training).
summary.explanation: Multimedia is widely used in teaching, games and films, marketing, and staff training.

summary.questionText: Explain the difference between raster and vector graphics.
summary.correctAnswer: Raster graphics are made of a grid of pixels and lose quality when enlarged, while vector graphics use mathematical lines and curves and can be resized without losing quality.
summary.explanation: The main difference is how the image is stored and how it behaves when scaled.

summary.questionText: Give two common file formats for images and two for audio.
summary.correctAnswer: Images: JPEG and PNG (also GIF, BMP). Audio: MP3 and WAV.
summary.explanation: Knowing which extension belongs to which media type helps in choosing the right format.

summary.questionText: What is meant by image resolution?
summary.correctAnswer: Resolution is the number of pixels that make up an image, usually written as width by height, such as 1920 x 1080.
summary.explanation: More pixels generally mean more detail and a larger file size.

summary.correctAnswer: Cropping, resizing, rotating, and colour adjustment.
summary.explanation: These basic operations let users improve and change the appearance of images.

summary.questionText: Name three hardware devices used in multimedia.
summary.correctAnswer: Scanner, camera, and speakers (also microphone and headphones).
summary.explanation: These devices help capture, input or output multimedia content.

summary.questionText: State one advantage and one challenge of using multimedia.
summary.correctAnswer: Advantage: it makes information more interesting and easier to understand. Challenge: multimedia files are large and need much storage space and powerful hardware.
summary.explanation: Multimedia improves communication but demands more resources.

summary.correctAnswer: Computer graphics is the creation, editing and display of images and pictures using a computer.
summary.explanation: It covers how computers produce and handle visual content such as drawings, photos and designs.

hoq.questionText: A graphic designer must create a company logo that will be printed both on a small business card and on a large billboard without becoming blurry. Which graphic type and format should be used?

options.text: A vector graphic, because it scales to any size without losing quality
A low-resolution JPEG raster image, because it has a small file size
A BMP bitmap, because it stores every pixel
A GIF, because it supports animation

hoq.explanation: Logos that must be resized to very different sizes should be vector graphics, since vectors can be scaled up or down without losing quality, unlike raster formats.

hoq.questionText: A student records a one-hour video lesson and finds the file is too large to send by email. Which action would BEST reduce the file size while keeping it as a video?

options.text: Save the video in a compressed format like MP4 at a lower resolution
Convert the video into a single JPEG image
Rename the file with a shorter name
Change the file extension from .avi to .txt

hoq.explanation: Using a compressed video format such as MP4 and lowering the resolution reduces file size while keeping it a playable video. Renaming or changing extensions to .txt does not reduce size or keep it usable, and a JPEG is not a video.

hoq.questionText: A photo of a building has too much empty sky at the top and looks slightly tilted. Which combination of editing operations should the user apply to fix both problems?

options.text: Cropping to remove the extra sky and rotating to straighten the image
Increasing the colour depth and changing the file format
Compressing the file and renaming it
Converting the image to audio and resizing it

hoq.explanation: Cropping removes the unwanted sky, and rotating straightens the tilted image. The other options do not address either the framing or the tilt.
